rationale: Use own colour and nearest nonzero colours up, down, left, and right. In demonstration 4, the top-right zero has only a downward neighbour colour 2 and becomes 7. In demonstration 10, the bottom-left zero sees 3 upward and 1 rightward and becomes 9. Other observed directional keys preserve their input colours.

Use own colour and zero-based row and column modulo 3. Zeros become 3 at residues (0,2), (2,1), and (2,2), and become 8 at (1,1); other residues and nonzero colours remain unchanged. Demonstration 1 shows 3 at (0,2), (2,2), and (3,2), and 8 at (1,1) and (4,1); demonstration 3 confirms the pattern across additional rows and columns.
